KEYS is a design enablement partner that sells design, emulation and test solutions across AI infrastructure, communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor and general electronics markets [D1]. The latest quarter, ended 2026-07-31, produced revenue of 1.85 billion, net income of 397 million, a gross margin of 65.87 percent and a net margin of 21.51 percent [D1]. The company reports two segments, with the Communications Solutions Group at 1.35 billion of revenue and 458 million of operating income and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group at 501 million of revenue and 155 million of operating income, giving total segment operating income of 613 million [D1]. Total assets were 11.92 billion, shareholders equity 6.57 billion and net debt 141 million [D1]. The shares are in an uptrend, with the close at 333.42 above the 20-day average of 330.47, the 50-day average of 326.21 and the 200-day average of 289.31, a 14-day relative strength index of 54.21, and a forward price to earnings of 20.66 against a trailing price to earnings of 45.89 and trailing earnings per share of 7.38 [D2].

What the market is arguing about is whether demand or supply sets the near-term number, because management said the supply environment is less flexible than a year ago, that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that conversion of demand into revenue will be nonlinear over the next several quarters [D3]. Management added that the bottleneck has shifted from internal capacity to external component supply, so revenue conversion stays nonlinear [D4]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat, which leaves a high comparison bar for profitability [D3].

On the chart that argument is unresolved, with the close of 333.42 sitting just above the high edge of immediate support at 332.78, an immediate support low edge at 300.87 and immediate resistance at 366.41, against a support strength of 59 and a resistance strength of three [D2]. The 14-day relative strength index of 54.21, a MACD of -1.45 against a signal of -1.84 with a histogram of 0.39, and an average true range of 11.05 describe the same stalemate [D2]. The largest marked move ran 28.62 percent from 2026-02-17 into 2026-02-24, and the most recent ran -13.98 percent from 2026-08-17 into 2026-08-24 [D2].

The plan is to let the next report settle which side is right, checking whether revenue holds at or above 1.85 billion [D1], whether gross margin holds at or above 65.87 percent and net margin at or above 21.51 percent [D1], and whether Communications Solutions Group revenue holds at or above 1.35 billion [D1]. Watch whether management repeats that supply chain is the governor of near-term revenue or drops the constraint language, and whether wireline keeps exceeding wireless [D3]. On the chart, a close below the support high edge of 332.78 and the support low edge of 300.87 would invalidate the uptrend, while a move to the resistance at 366.41 would confirm it [D2].
